grade.rationale: The API is compact, readable, and builds successfully according to the supplied analyzer evidence. Its main weaknesses are weakly typed provenance fields and registry construction that exposes incidental collection exceptions instead of clear domain validation.

summary: The sensor abstractions are generally clear and maintainable, with sensible cancellation support and deterministic registry ordering. Strengthening provenance types and validating sensor registrations would prevent invalid metadata and improve startup diagnostics and testability. Test coverage is unknown.

grade.rationale: The principal contracts are coherent, but provenance can contain invalid scope and timestamp values because those fields are represented as unconstrained strings.
The small records and interfaces are easy to evolve, although duplicating the scope concept as both an enum and a string creates avoidable conversion and validation work.
Names and signatures communicate intent well, but generic exceptions during registry construction do not clearly identify malformed or conflicting registrations.
Missing lookups receive a domain-specific exception, while null sensors and duplicate or invalid IDs fail through incidental LINQ or dictionary exceptions without tailored diagnostics.

Interfaces and immutable-looking result models are straightforward to fake and assert against; stronger provenance types would further reduce validation cases and ambiguous timestamp comparisons. Coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Provenance timestamps are stored as unvalidated strings
findings.description: `ScannedAt` accepts any string, so sensors can emit malformed timestamps, timestamps without an offset, or inconsistent formats. Consumers must repeatedly parse and validate the value, and chronological comparisons may be unreliable.
findings.recommendation: Represent the value as `DateTimeOffset` (or `Instant` if the project uses Noda Time), and serialize it in a standardized format only at persistence or transport boundaries.

findings.title: Provenance duplicates the typed scope as a free-form string
findings.description: The model defines `SensorScope` but stores provenance scope as `string`. This permits unsupported values and creates conversion code, spelling differences, and possible disagreement between the request scope and recorded provenance.
findings.recommendation: Change `SensorProvenance.Scope` to `SensorScope`; perform any required textual serialization at the system boundary.

findings.title: Registry construction relies on incidental dictionary exceptions
findings.description: The constructor does not explicitly validate the sensor sequence, entries, or IDs. A null entry causes a `NullReferenceException`, while duplicate IDs—including IDs differing only by case—cause a generic `ArgumentException`. These failures provide less actionable configuration diagnostics than the domain-specific lookup error.
findings.recommendation: Guard against a null collection, null entries, and null, empty, or whitespace IDs; detect case-insensitive duplicates explicitly and throw a dedicated registration/configuration exception that names the conflicting ID.
